summary: Volkbert Näther is an indologist and tibetologist. He earned his doctorate at the University of Marburg, where he studied under Claus Vogel (attested 1975).

Volker Caumanns specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under David P. Jackson at the University of Hamburg and Franz-Karl Ehrhard at the University of Munich, where he was a research assistant (2006–2012) before posts at LIRI and the University of Bern.

Volker Grabowsky is a historian and scholar of Buddhist studies. Educated at Kiel, Chiang Mai, and Hamburg, he held posts at Passau, Hamburg, the National University of Laos, and Münster, before becoming chair of Thai language and culture at Hamburg in 2009.

Volker Zotz works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Vienna and under Anagarika Govinda, later holding academic positions at Vienna, Otani University, Ryukoku University, Saarland University, and the University of Luxembourg.
W. F. Jayasuriya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne (attested 1963) and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

W. H. D. Rouse was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Cheltenham, Regent's Park, and Cambridge. A fellow at Christ's College, he taught at Bedford, Cheltenham, and Rugby before serving as headmaster of The Perse School (1902–1928).

W. H. R. Rivers was a British scholar of history and archaeology. After medical studies at St Bartholomew's and the University of London, he worked at several hospitals, taught at Cambridge and UCL, and served as president of the Anthropological Society of London.

W. Norman Brown was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Maurice Bloomfield at Johns Hopkins and Franklin Edgerton. He spent most of his career at the University of Pennsylvania (1926–1966) and served as Indian art curator at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

W. Randolph Kloetzli is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago in 1964 and lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

W. S. Karunatillake was a scholar of linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was a Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.

Wai-lun Tam is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. He became a professor and department chairperson at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Walpola Rahula was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied in Ceylon, Calcutta, and Paris under Paul Demiéville. He was a professor at Northwestern University, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, and held a post at Oxford.

Walter Bruno Henning was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Göttingen, he held academic appointments at SOAS University of London, Columbia University, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Walter Elliot was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College and the College of Fort St George, later serving as Private Secretary to Lord Elphinstone in the Government of Madras (1837–1842).

Walter Eugene Clark was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from Harvard and studied with Richard Pischel. He taught at the University of Chicago before serving as Wales Professor of Sanskrit at Harvard (1927–1950).

Walter Evans-Wentz was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Stanford University and the University of Oxford (Jesus College) and later studied under Kazi Dawa Samdup from approximately 1919 to 1922.

Walter Liebenthal was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who earned his doctorate at Breslau. He taught at Peking University, held research and visiting positions at Visva-Bharati, and was an honorary professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Tübingen.

Walter M. Spink was an Indologist and art historian educated at Amherst College and Harvard University (PhD 1954). He taught at Brandeis University before serving as a professor at the University of Michigan from around 1961 to 2000.

Walter Nowick was a Buddhist studies figure who attended the Juilliard School and studied under Zuigan Goto from 1950 to 1965. He held a post at Kyoto Women's University and founded Moonspring Hermitage.
Walter Piston studied at the Massachusetts College of Art and Design and Harvard University. He held an academic post at Harvard University from approximately 1926 to 1960.
